name: NTUC Health Senior Day Care (Toa Payoh)
description: General full-day day care for seniors who need supervision, meals and company while the caregiver works or takes a break. Activities include group exercise, art and craft, karaoke and outings, with nurses on site to help with medication and basic health checks. Round-trip transport is offered within about 5km of the centre. Fees shown are the approximate full monthly rate broken down per day before means-tested subsidy; households with per-capita income of S$2,600 or below can receive up to 80% off through AIC. Best for a frail or lonely senior who is still fairly mobile and does not have significant dementia-related behaviours.

name: New Horizon Centre (Toa Payoh) - Dementia Singapore
description: Dementia-specific day care run by Dementia Singapore, in the same neighbourhood as several general day centres but built around memory loss. Multidisciplinary team of doctors, nurses, occupational therapists and physiotherapists. Structured routine with reminiscence activities, music, gentle exercise and cognitive stimulation, and staff trained to de-escalate agitation, sundowning and wandering. Also runs an Early Dementia Programme for seniors recently diagnosed and still quite independent. Choose this over a general day centre when confusion, repetitive questioning or resistance to care is the main challenge.

name: New Horizon Centre (Bukit Batok) - Dementia Singapore
description: West-side dementia day care with the same programme as the other New Horizon Centres: a calm, predictable daily structure, small activity groups, and a team of nurses, occupational therapists and physiotherapists. Suited to early-to-moderate dementia, including seniors who get anxious or agitated in noisy, unfamiliar places. Includes the Early Dementia Programme for the newly diagnosed. Good option for a caregiver living around Bukit Batok, Jurong or Choa Chu Kang who needs weekday cover.

name: New Horizon Centre (Tampines) - Dementia Singapore
description: East-side dementia day care from Dementia Singapore, covering Tampines, Pasir Ris and Bedok. Same structured, dementia-trained model: reminiscence and sensory activities, gentle physical exercise, and staff who can manage confusion, agitation and wandering without restraint. Runs the Early Dementia Programme as well. Weekday hours are long enough to cover a full working day plus commute.

name: NTUC Health Senior Day Care (Chai Chee) - Dementia Care
description: Day care in the Chai Chee / Bedok area with a dedicated dementia care track and unusually flexible attendance - you can book half-days or specific weekdays rather than a fixed five-day package, and Saturday cover is available. Helpful when the caregiver only needs a few hours on certain days, or is easing a resistant parent into day care gradually. Nurses on site; transport within roughly 5km. Fees are approximate full rate per day before AIC means-tested subsidy.

name: Apex Harmony Lodge Dementia Day Care Centre (Pasir Ris)
description: Day care attached to Singapore's first purpose-built dementia home, set on a large Pasir Ris site with secure landscaped gardens and courtyards a resident can walk freely without getting lost. Receives MOH subvention as subsidised step-down care, so the daily fee is much lower than most day centres. Designed for moderate-to-advanced dementia, including seniors who pace, wander or have exit-seeking behaviour that a shophouse-unit day centre cannot safely contain. Access is usually via an AIC or hospital referral.

name: St Luke's ElderCare Senior Care Centre (Teck Whye)
description: Combined day care and day rehabilitation centre in the Teck Whye / Choa Chu Kang area. Alongside supervision and activities it has physiotherapists and occupational therapists on site, so it suits a senior recovering function after a stroke, fall or hospital stay who needs rehab and a caregiver break in one place. Admission is open to Singaporeans, PRs and foreigners aged 50 and above. Saturday attendance is available. Fee is approximate before subsidy.

name: St Luke's ElderCare Weekend Respite Care (Bishan)
description: Weekend-only centre-based respite for caregivers whose weekdays are already covered (by a helper, a weekday day centre, or family) but who have no relief on Saturdays and Sundays. Runs a full day of supervised activities and meals. Citizen out-of-pocket is roughly S$15.60 to S$19.60 per attendance, making it one of the cheapest respite options. Also useful as a low-commitment trial before signing up for a full weekday day-care package.

name: Homage Home-Based Respite Care
days: Daily, including weekends and public holidays
hours: flexible, from 1-hour visits; overnight and 24-hour available
area: Islandwide (care worker travels to the home)
description: A vetted care professional comes to the senior's own home, so nobody has to travel or adjust to a new place. Covers help with bathing, dressing, toileting, transfers, meal preparation, medication reminders, companionship and light exercise; nurses can be requested for higher needs. Booking is flexible from a single hour up to overnight and 24-hour shifts. The best fit when the senior is bedbound, has limited mobility, refuses point-blank to leave the house, or when the caregiver just needs a few covered hours at short notice. Daily-living care starts around S$23 per hour before the Home Caregiving Grant; the figure shown is a typical four-hour visit.

name: NTUC Health Night Respite / Staycay@Henderson
description: Overnight-only respite for the situation daytime care does not solve: a senior with dementia who is up, disoriented and restless through the night, leaving the caregiver unable to sleep. Furnished room with daily housekeeping, laundry, weekly exercise and a nursing aide on call 24/7. Roughly S$80 to S$120 per night before subsidy. Use it for a run of nights to let an exhausted caregiver recover, or around the caregiver's own night-shift work or medical procedure.

name: NTUC Health Nursing Home Respite (Jurong)
days: By arrangement, minimum a few days
hours: 24-hour residential, up to 30 days per stay
description: Short residential stay in a nursing home, up to about 30 days, with 24/7 skilled nursing, medication management and rehab support. This is the option for an extended caregiver absence - overseas travel, the caregiver's own surgery and recovery, or simply a longer breakdown-prevention break. Handles higher-acuity needs including incontinence care, feeding assistance and fall risk that day or home respite cannot. Around S$100 to S$150 per day before subsidy; needs a doctor's referral. Book well ahead as places are limited.

name: All Saints Home Respite Care (Hougang)
hours: 24-hour residential, minimum 7 days, up to 30 days per year
description: Nursing-home respite on the north-east side, with sister homes in Tampines, Yishun and Jurong East. Stays run from a one-week minimum up to 30 days a year. Round-the-clock nursing, suitable for post-hospital step-down recovery or a planned caregiver break. A good north-east alternative when Hougang, Sengkang or Punggol is more reachable for family visits than a west-side home. Approximate daily rate before means-tested subsidy.

name: AWWA Dementia Day Care Centre (Yishun)
description: Dementia day care in the far north, covering Yishun, Sembawang and Woodlands. Multidisciplinary team, individual care plans, and a programme of cognitive and sensory activities with physiotherapy input. Staff are trained for dementia-related agitation and wandering. Fills the gap for northern caregivers who would otherwise face a long daily trip to a dementia centre in Toa Payoh or Bukit Batok. Approximate full daily fee before AIC subsidy.
